question.text: How many turkey poults will USDA NASS report as net placed in the United States during October 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the October 2026 net poult placements figure published in USDA NASS's [Turkey Hatchery](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/publication/turkey-hatchery) report scheduled for release at 3:00 p.m. ET on November 13, 2026. Use the value for October 2026 in the report's net poult placements table for the United States (total all breeds), which NASS publishes in thousands of poults; for example, a reported figure of 19,571 thousand poults resolves as 19,571. The figure as first published in that report governs, and revisions published in later NASS reports do not change the resolution. If the report does not include an October 2026 placement estimate, resolution waits for the next NASS report that contains it.
question.fine_print:
- Use NASS's published estimate as-is, including all breeds; do not adjust it for exports, deaths in transit, or any other factor.
- The other figures in the same report (turkey eggs in incubators on November 1, poults hatched in October, percentages of a year earlier) are context only and are not the resolution value.
- Only the October 2026 placement figure counts, not the September or November estimates or the November 1 eggs-in-incubators value.

# NASS October 2026 net poult placements: research brief

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-13: NASS's [ESMIS Turkey Hatchery page](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/publication/turkey-hatchery) lists the next release for Nov 13, 2026 at 3:00 PM, then Dec 14, 2026.
- 2026-10-13: The latest report ([tkha1026.txt](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/sites/default/release-files/796103/tkha1026.txt)) shows September 2026 net placements of 19,571 thousand, up 2% from 19,096. The October 2026 cell is blank. The 2025-26 column has October 2025 at 21,284 and November 2025 at 18,482.
- Leading indicators in the same report:
  - Eggs in incubators on Oct 1, 2026: 26,695 thousand, against 26,122 a year earlier (+2%).
  - Poults hatched in September 2026: 21,122. October 2025 hatch was 22,981.
- Reliability: the root mean square error (RMSE) for placements is 4.2%, with a 90% band of ±7.1%. The average first-to-latest revision is 678 thousand, and the largest is 1,775 thousand. [tkha1026](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/sites/default/release-files/796103/tkha1026.txt)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles this yet. NASS has not published an October 2026 figure.
- One caveat on the comparison base: the 21,284 for October 2025 is a revised number. The first published value was 19,684 (Dec 2025 report). It was raised about 8% in the April 2026 annual revision. October 2024 went the same way, from 19,510 first published to 20,165 revised. [Dec 2025](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/sites/default/release-files/795687/tkha1225.txt), [Mar 2026](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/sites/default/release-files/795821/tkha0326.txt), [Apr 2026](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/sites/default/release-files/795858/tkha0426.txt)
- So year-over-year percentages in 2026 reports compare first prints against revised 2025 values. First-print October numbers have come in well below the later revised values.
- The October and November 2025 reports are not on the ESMIS list. October 2025 first appeared in the December 2025 report, which I believe was because of the autumn 2025 government shutdown.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-28/29: H5N1 was confirmed in a commercial turkey flock of about 44,400 birds in Sac County, Iowa. It is Iowa's first commercial case in nearly a year, and the county is under a disaster declaration through Nov 27. [Iowa Ag](https://iowaagriculture.gov/news/HPAI-sac-county-10-28-2026), [Iowa Capital Dispatch](https://iowacapitaldispatch.com/2026/10/29/bird-flu-detected-in-iowa-commercial-flock-for-first-time-nearly-a-year/)
- 2026-10-27: A Morrison County, Minnesota flock of about 61,000 commercial turkey meat birds was reported. [Willmar Radio](https://www.willmarradio.com/news/bird-flu-found-in-morrison-county-flock/article_9ef8c068-1233-436e-bc71-6e1e9fcafe6e.html)
- 2026-10-22: APHIS confirmed turkey flocks of 57,500 birds in Minnesota and 13,500 in Wisconsin. The Wisconsin flock was a Barron County breeder hen flock, which matters for egg supply rather than grow-out. Minnesota is at 20 commercial flocks this year and Wisconsin at 6. [WATTPoultry](https://www.wattagnet.com/poultry-meat/diseases-health/avian-influenza/news/15975553/aphis-confirms-avian-flu-cases-in-minnesota-wisconsin)
- 2026-10-21: A Dickey County, North Dakota flock of 60,600 birds was reported, according to the question background. I did not verify this independently.
- 2026-10: The October 2026 ERS Livestock, Dairy, and Poultry Outlook page has no turkey details. I could not see its turkey forecast. [ERS](https://ers.usda.gov/publications/115633)

## 4. Base rates

**October placements by year**

| Year | Value (thousand poults) | Note |
|---|---|---|
| 2023 | 20,895 | |
| 2024 | 20,165 | revised (first print 19,510) |
| 2025 | 21,284 | revised (first print 19,684) |

[Sep 2025](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/sites/default/release-files/k643b117x/m326p167w/76539164w/tkha0925.txt), [Apr 2026](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/sites/default/release-files/795858/tkha0426.txt)

**September-to-October change**
- 2023: +9.4%
- 2024: +8.4% revised
- 2025: +11.5% revised, or +8.3% on first prints (18,179 to 19,684)

**Recent 2026 months**
- Placements: June 19,735, July 21,031, August 21,164 (revised from 21,213, +7% YoY), September 19,571 (+2% YoY).
- Hatch: July 21,365, August 21,873 (+8%), September 21,122 (+2%).

**Placements as a share of hatch**
- 0.926 in October 2025, 0.927 in September 2026, 0.968 in August 2026.

**Hatch as a share of eggs in incubators on the 1st of the month**
- October 2025: 0.88 (26,122 eggs to 22,981 poults).
- September 2026: 0.84 on first prints (25,174 eggs to 21,122 poults).

**Illustrative arithmetic only, not a forecast**
- 26,695 eggs × 0.84-0.88 gives an implied hatch of 22.4-23.5 million.
- That hatch × 0.93 gives 20.8-21.8 million placements.
- A +11% step from September's 19,571 gives about 21,720.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Kalshi, Polymarket, Manifold or Metaculus market on turkey poult placements.
- The Kalshi markets supplied with this question (Vermont milk, corn yield and others) are unrelated.
- I found no analyst estimate of October 2026 placements.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-13, 3:00 PM ET: the NASS Turkey Hatchery release, which resolves the question. It will also revise September 2026. [ESMIS](https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/publication/turkey-hatchery)
- Ongoing: possible further APHIS HPAI turkey confirmations, though October placements are already done. Late-October outbreaks in Minnesota, Iowa, North Dakota and Wisconsin may have delayed some placements into barns that were depopulated or under control-area restrictions.
- The government-shutdown risk around the midterms is not confirmed. A shutdown would delay the release, as happened in autumn 2025.
- Mid-November: the ERS outlook and WASDE turkey projections come out, but they don't affect the resolution value.

(a) About 11 days. NASS releases the figure on November 13, 2026 at 3:00 p.m. ET.

(b) The latest value is September 2026 net placements of 19,571 thousand, first print, from the October 13, 2026 report. Eggs in incubators on October 1 were 26,695 thousand, up 2% from a year earlier.

(c) If nothing changed, October would equal September's 19,571. That is unrealistic because October is seasonally higher.

(d) If the usual seasonal step and current trend hold, the estimate is about 20,900 to 21,700:
- The September-to-October step on first prints was +8.3% in 2025, which gives about 21,200.
- Eggs in incubators times the usual hatch rate times the placement ratio gives about 20,800 to 21,800.
- Year over year, +2% on October 2025's revised 21,284 gives about 21,700.
- Two things pull the estimate lower. First-print October values have come in well below revised ones (19,510 in 2024 and 19,684 in 2025). Late-October H5N1 disruptions may also have deferred some placements.

(e) The September-to-October step has run about +8% to +11.5%. NASS's own error is an RMSE of 4.2%, or about ±900 thousand, and first prints have been revised by up to 1,775 thousand.

(f) I found no market or analyst forecast. The implied consensus is around 21,000.

(g) Low scenario: HPAI control areas in Minnesota, Iowa and North Dakota delay placements, and the first print comes in conservative, as in prior Octobers, at about 19,500. Combined with these, a weak survey response could go below 19,000. High scenario: a strong hatch from the high egg sets (about 23.5 million) plus producers refilling barns for the holidays could push placements toward 22,500 or more.

(b) Latest known value: September 2026 net poult placements were 19,571 thousand (first print, released October 13, 2026). Eggs in incubators on October 1 were 26,695 thousand, up 2% year over year.

(c) If nothing changed: a flat carry-over of September gives about 19,571. That ignores the strong seasonal rise into October, so it is an unrealistic anchor.

- **H5N1.** The late-October outbreaks involved roughly 250,000 birds, most of them grow-out turkeys plus one breeder flock. This is a small downward nudge against a 21 million base.
- My central estimate is about 21,100.

(e) Historical variation:
- October levels over 2023 to 2025 ranged from about 19,500 to 21,300, depending on whether first prints or revised values are used.
- NASS's RMSE is 4.2%, about 890 thousand.
- Uncertainty from the leading indicators is roughly ±4 to 5% (one standard deviation about 800 to 900).

(f) Experts and markets: there are no markets and no analyst estimates for this figure. The ERS outlook did not provide turkey detail.

(g) Unexpected scenarios:
- **Low:** H5N1 control areas in Minnesota, Iowa and North Dakota plus integrators trimming placements because of weak margins lead NASS to print a soft first estimate, similar to the 19,510 and 19,684 first prints of 2024 and 2025. That would put the figure around 19,000 to 19,500, or lower in an extreme case.
- **High:** a strong hatch from the large October 1 egg set, with unaffected producers filling holiday demand, pushes the figure to 22,500 to 23,000.

**(d) Outcome if the trend continued:**

- The NASS root mean square error is 4.2%, or about 900 thousand.
- The October/September ratio has been fairly stable, roughly plus or minus 1.5% across years.
- Combined with survey noise, I use a standard deviation of about 800 to 900 thousand.

**(f) Experts and markets:** I found no markets or analyst forecasts for this figure.

**(g) Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** HPAI control areas in Minnesota, Iowa and the Dakotas defer placements broadly, the Wisconsin breeder loss trims supply, and the first print undercounts as it did for October 2025. Placements would then come in around 19,000 to 19,500.
- **High:** unaffected producers front-load placements, and the hatch converts strongly from the 8% jump in eggs set. Placements would then come in around 22,800 to 23,500.
